note: Round thirteen: search by meaning (embeddings) in the document-answering assistant. Expected results written before any code, on 25 Oct 2026. The question is whether the round-nine permission controls still hold when documents are found by meaning instead of keywords. Round nine used keyword matching. The embedding model is a stand-in in the sandbox and is meant to be a real local model on the Mac; the first-run result records which one. The AI model that writes answers is not tested.

cases.title: Support agent asks about pay in words that share no keyword with the HR salary document. Asked with no permission check, and with the live permission check before retrieval
cases.expected_in_words: With no check, search by meaning finds the HR salary document that keyword search would have missed, and its text reaches the support agent; with the live check before retrieval, it does not. This assumes the model ranks that document in its top three, which depends on the model

cases.title: The same question, with the permission check in place, when the answer shows its sources. Asked when the source list shows every match, and when it shows only what the person may see
cases.expected_in_words: The title of the HR document appears in the source list when every match is shown, and does not when only allowed sources are shown

cases.title: Search keeps only the best match (top one) and the best match is a restricted document. Asked when the permission filter runs after the ranking, and when it runs before
cases.expected_in_words: With the filter after the ranking, the person gets nothing at all (no leak, but no answer); with the filter before, they get the best document they may see

cases.title: A customer note holds an Aadhaar number and is found by meaning. Asked with the number masked when the notes are indexed, and without masking
cases.expected_in_words: Without masking the number appears in the answer; with masking it appears as [AADHAAR]. The masking does not depend on how the document was found

cases.title: An HR person moves to Support, and then asks about pay by meaning. Asked when permissions are checked against the copy taken at indexing time, and against the live directory
cases.expected_in_words: With the copy from indexing time the former HR person still sees HR text; with the live directory they do not. The result is the same as with keyword search

cases.title: Two documents each open to everyone: one says who sits on a panel, the other what that panel's members are paid. Asked by meaning how much the named person earns. All the live checks are on
cases.expected_in_words: Both documents are found by meaning and the answer puts the two facts together; no control here sees it. This is a limit, not a control
